sourcedFrom: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 (01/2011 (printed as the document code G0110601 - C - 01/2011; no separate © line))
cleanIntro: Benelli's own strip for the NOVA Pump Action, in Benelli's order. This is a pump gun with a rotating locking head — the bolt locks into the barrel extension the way a semi-auto's does, so the bolt group that comes out looks nothing like a traditional pump's. Nine steps take it to bare parts including the firing pin, and the manual says outright when it is finished. One trap on reassembly: the two trigger guard pins are different lengths and the longer one has a place.

steps.title: Confirm which Nova this is — this manual covers the NOVA Pump Action, not the NOVA 3
steps.action: Check the gun and its paperwork. This book introduces itself as the manual for the "NOVA Pump Action" shotgun, in 12 and 20 gauge. Benelli publishes a separate owner's manual for the NOVA 3, which is a different and later gun.
steps.prose: The catalog says only "Nova", and Benelli has used that name across more than one design. This book's own cover lists exactly two products — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) and Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — and its introduction names the shotgun the same way. If your gun is a NOVA 3 the strip below does not describe it and you need that separate manual instead. This is worth thirty seconds now rather than a part in your hand that does not match the page.
steps.quote:
Thank you for selecting one of 
our products: 
the “NOVA Pump Action” shotgun!
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Introduction — p.30

steps.title: Safety catch on — the red ring must disappear
steps.action: Press the crossbolt safety button on the trigger guard until the red ring is no longer visible.
steps.prose: Benelli defines the safe state by what you cannot see rather than by which way the button points. Red showing means it will fire, and on a pump gun that you are about to work the action on repeatedly, that check comes before anything else.
steps.quote: Press the safety button on the trigger guard until its red ring, indicating firing position, is no longer visible (fig. 2A - 2B).
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Safety catch — p.32

steps.title: Chambered round out by hand, muzzle safe, fingers off the trigger
steps.action: With the safety engaged and the muzzle pointed somewhere safe, depress the breech bolt latch and pull the fore-end slowly rearward until the cartridge is out of the chamber and lying on the carrier. Turn the gun toward the ejection port and take the cartridge out.
steps.prose: Slowly and partially is the whole instruction — run the fore-end back briskly and the round is flung out of the port instead of presented to you, which is fine on a range and not fine over a hard floor. The breech bolt latch has to be pressed first or the action will not open on a closed bolt.
steps.quote: Engage the safety. Depress the breech bolt latch; slowly pull the fore-end rearward until the cartridge is extracted from the chamber and is resting inside the action on the carrier. Turn the firearm toward the ejection port side and remove the cartridge.
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Unloading — manual unloading, step 1, p.50

steps.title: Now empty the magazine tube, one shell at a time
steps.action: Push the fore-end fully forward to close the bolt on an empty chamber. Turn the gun over, thrust the carrier inward, and press the cartridge retaining lever from the front with your index finger. One shell releases per press. Repeat until the tube is empty, then confirm barrel, carrier and magazine are all empty.
steps.prose: An empty chamber on a pump gun means nothing while the tube is loaded — the next stroke of the fore-end chambers a live round, and the strip below starts with a stroke of the fore-end. Benelli's own check at the end of this step names three places to look, not one.
steps.quote: Check that the barrel, carrier, and magazine are completely empty.
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Unloading — manual unloading, step 4, p.52
steps.warn: WARNING: the ejected cartridges will fall to the ground. Ensure that they fall to a safe place.

steps.title: Prove it empty once more before a single part moves
steps.action: Before starting any part of the strip, make sure the chamber and the magazine are unloaded. Read the loading and unloading instructions if you are at all unsure.
steps.prose: Benelli reprints this warning at the head of the stripping section rather than trusting the clearing section to have done its job, and it is the right instinct: the gun has been handled, turned over and worked since you cleared it.
steps.quote: Before starting any operation on your shotgun, make sure that the chamber and the magazine are unloaded! (Carefully read the instructions on gun loading and unloading).
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Shotgun stripping (for cleaning and maintenance) — p.62

steps.title: Bolt forward, barrel retaining cap off
steps.action: Move the bolt forward, then unscrew the barrel retaining cap from the end of the magazine tube.
steps.prose: The bolt goes forward first because the cap will not clear a bolt that is back — and because you want the action closed while you are turning a cap against spring pressure. Keep the cap: it is a tool in two steps' time.
steps.quote: Move the bolt forward and unscrew the barrel retaining cap (fig. 20).
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 1, p.62

steps.title: Barrel forward off the magazine tube
steps.action: Take hold of the barrel where it stands clear of the magazine tube and slide it straight forward off the gun.
steps.prose: Straight forward, holding it out from the tube. The Nova's barrel extension carries the locking recesses the bolt head turns into, so the surfaces you are sliding apart here are the ones that hold pressure — do not lever the barrel sideways to start it.
steps.quote: Hold the barrel out from the magazine tube and slide it forward  (fig. 21).
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 2, p.64

steps.title: Trigger guard pins out — using the magazine cap as the tool
steps.action: Use the magazine cap, which has a peg on its front face, to push the two trigger guard fixing pins out. Still using the cap, hook them and draw them clear of their seats. Then take the trigger guard off.
steps.prose: This is why the cap was worth keeping: Benelli built the punch into it, so there is no excuse for a screwdriver near those pins. Note that the two pins are NOT the same — their lengths differ, and getting them back in the right holes is called out separately in the assembly section.
steps.quote: Using the magazine cap, push out the trigger guard fixing pins and - still using the magazine cap - hook them and take them off of their places (figs. 22-23).
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 3, p.64

steps.title: Gun reversed, action bars lifted, slide pulled back to separate
steps.action: Turn the shotgun over, lift the action bars slightly, and at the same time pull the slide back to separate the two.
steps.prose: Both hands are doing different things at once here, and that is deliberate — the action bars hook onto the bolt guide and only release when they are lifted off it, so pulling straight back without the lift just drags the whole assembly. It is the same interlock in reverse on reassembly, where the manual has you check the engagement.
steps.quote: Reverse the shotgun, lift the action bars slightly, and pull back the slide at the same time to separate the action bars (fig. 25).
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 5, p.66

steps.title: Bolt unit off the receiver by compressing its head
steps.action: Hold the bolt unit and push the top of it, then take the unit off the receiver.
steps.prose: That push is compressing the rotating locking head back into the bolt body. The Nova locks like a semi-auto — a head that turns lugs into the barrel extension — and until the head is pushed in, the unit will not clear its channel.
steps.quote: hold the bolt unit and, pushing the top, take it off of the receiver (figs. 26-27).
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 6, p.66

steps.title: Fore-end forward and off, unhooking the action bars
steps.action: Slide the fore-end forward slowly, unhooking the action bars from the receiver.
steps.prose: Slowly, because the bars are still in their tracks in the receiver for the first part of the travel and they will bind if the fore-end is twisted while it comes.
steps.quote: Slide the fore-end forward slowly, unhooking the action bars from the receiver (fig. 28).
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 7, p.66

steps.title: Firing pin out — only when it needs it
steps.action: If the firing pin needs cleaning, remove its retaining pin while holding the firing pin and its return spring, then draw the firing pin out complete with its spring.
steps.prose: Benelli says "when necessary" rather than "always", and the maintenance section explains why it ever becomes necessary: powder residue collects on the firing pin the same way it does in the trigger group. Hold it as the retaining pin comes out — there is a spring behind it.
steps.quote: When necessary, proceed with the disassembly of the firing pin, removing the retaining pin (fig. 29); hold the firing pin and its return spring.
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 8, p.68

steps.title: Strip complete — Benelli says so in as many words
steps.action: You have the barrel, the magazine cap, the trigger guard with its two pins, the bolt unit, the fore-end with its action bars, the stock-receiver, and the firing pin with its spring. That is the whole of the published teardown.
steps.prose: There is no deeper published procedure in this book — the trigger group is removed as a unit and is not taken apart at this level, and the rotating head is left in the bolt. What you have on the bench is exactly what Benelli intends you to clean.
steps.quote: The shotgun is now completely stripped. All the parts that require routine maintenance and cleaning are disassembled.
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Stripping procedure, after step 9, p.68

steps.title: Barrel first, and leave the choke tube in it
steps.action: Clean the bore normally after use. Do NOT unscrew the internal choke tube to do it.
steps.prose: That note reverses what most people assume. Taking the choke out to clean behind it is exactly how residue gets into the choke threads inside the barrel, and those threads are far more annoying to clean than the bore ever is.
steps.quote: NOTE: whilst cleaning the gun the internal choke tubes are not to be stripped out. This in order to avoid residues collecting in the barrel’s internal choke tube’s connection threads.
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Maintenance — note, p.60

steps.title: Bolt unit and trigger group: periodic cleaning of powder residue
steps.action: Take the bolt assembly down, clean and lubricate it on a schedule. Do the same for the firing mechanism — hammer, trigger and the rest of the group — which clogs with the same residue.
steps.prose: Benelli's position is that these guns need no special maintenance, only that the two places powder residue collects get attention on a schedule rather than on a hunch. Note the manual's own text here is the shared Benelli boilerplate and says "Automatic Shotguns" even in this pump gun's book; the items it lists are the ones this gun has.
steps.quote: the bolt assembly may also become clogged with the same material and must be periodically dismantled, cleaned and lubricated;
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Maintenance, item 3, p.58

steps.title: Oil what the weather can reach, with Benelli's own oil
steps.action: Lightly oil the parts exposed to the atmosphere to keep the gun in good order. Benelli specifies its own cleaning set and oil, which is not supplied with the shotgun.
steps.prose: This is the anti-corrosion pass, not the lubrication pass — a wiped film on external steel. Flooding the trigger group with oil in the name of protection is how a pump gun collects a paste of oil and powder in exactly the place item 2 told you to keep clean.
steps.quote: to keep the gun in good order, oiling of the parts subject to atmospheric corrosion is recommended.
steps.cite: Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — Nova Pump Action (cal. 12) / Nova Pump Action (cal. 20) — G0110601 - C - 01/2011 — Maintenance, item 4, p.60

deepAbsentReason: This book publishes ONE teardown, headed "Shotgun stripping (for cleaning and maintenance)", and closes it with "The shotgun is now completely stripped". It already reaches the firing pin and its spring. There is no further published user-level disassembly for the Nova to promote into a deep clean, and the trigger group is removed and refitted as a unit throughout.

cleaning.name: Barrel
tasks: Normal cleaning of the bore after use.
Leave the internal choke tube installed while cleaning — removing it lets residue into the choke threads inside the barrel.
Benelli Armi cleaning set and oil only (not supplied with the shotgun).

cleaning.name: Trigger group
tasks: Hammer, trigger and the rest of the firing mechanism cleaned of powder residue and foreign matter.
Periodic cleaning or lubrication — the group comes out as a unit and is not taken apart at this level.

cleaning.name: Bolt unit
tasks: Dismantled, cleaned and lubricated periodically — it clogs with the same residue as the trigger group.
Rotating locking head and its channel in the bolt body.
Firing pin and its return spring, when residue has reached them.

cleaning.name: External surfaces
tasks: Light oil on parts subject to atmospheric corrosion.

reassembly: Firing pin complete with its spring back into the bolt, fixed with its pin.
Bolt taken by the top part and squeezed, then inserted in its proper place.
Firearm held vertically; the fore-end guide rods inserted in their respective tracks.
Firearm laid horizontal; the action bars hooked onto the bolt guide, lifting the bars slightly with the other hand.
CHECK the action bars-to-bolt engagement is correct before going further.
Fore-end slid ahead; trigger guard inserted with the hammer COCKED, twisting in at the front locking hole and then seating the rear on the receiver.
Trigger guard pins pushed in — the LONGER pin goes in the forward hole.
Barrel and barrel retaining cap refitted to complete the assembly.
fncheck: With the gun proven empty: check the action bars-to-bolt engagement is correct before the trigger guard goes back, because it cannot be seen afterwards. Refit the trigger guard only with the hammer cocked. With everything together, press the safety button until the red ring disappears and confirm it does, work the fore-end fully back and forward to confirm the bolt runs and locks, and check the barrel retaining cap is fully screwed down onto the magazine tube.
